questions.question: Which ruler regained his lost kingdom by 1555 after defeating Sher Shah Suri's successors, thereby marking the end of the Second Afghan Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humayun**__.

• He recaptured Delhi and Agra from the Afghan rulers, marking the end of the **Second Afghan Empire**.
 
• Humayun's return to power was aided by strategic alliances, including support from the Persian ruler Shah Tahmasp.
 
• His victory restored the Mughal Empire's presence in India, laying the foundation for the reign of his son, Akbar the Great.
 
• Humayun's return to the throne was short-lived, as he passed away in 1556, shortly after regaining power.

• Sher Shah's successors were unable to maintain control, leading to Humayun's return.
 
 
 
• **Shah Tahmasp's Support:**
 
 
• Humayun sought refuge in Persia after losing his kingdom and received military assistance from Shah Tahmasp.
 
• This alliance was pivotal in Humayun's successful campaign against the Afghan rulers.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Empire:**
 
 
• The Mughal Empire was one of the largest and most influential empires in Indian history, known for its cultural and architectural contributions.

questions.question: What is the primary function of an operating system in a laptop?

options.text: To manage hardware and software resources

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To manage hardware and software resources**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An operating system acts as an intermediary between **hardware and software**, enabling them to function together seamlessly.
 
• Its primary role is to manage **system resources**, such as CPU, memory, storage, and input/output devices.
 
• The operating system provides a **user interface** (e.g., command line or graphical user interface) to interact with the system.
 
• It oversees tasks like **process scheduling**, ensuring efficient execution of multiple programs.
 
• Popular operating systems include Windows, macOS, Linux, and Chrome OS, each designed to optimize resource utilization and user experience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kernel:**

 
 
• The kernel is the core component of an operating system, responsible for **managing system resources** and facilitating communication between hardware and software.
 
• It handles essential functions like **memory management, process management, and device control.**
 
 
 
• **File System:**
 
 
• The operating system organizes and stores data using a **file system**, enabling efficient retrieval and management.
 
• Popular file systems include **NTFS, FAT32, ext4, and APFS**.
 
 
 
• **Multitasking:**
 
 
• Modern operating systems support **multitasking**, allowing multiple processes to run simultaneously.
 
• This is achieved through process scheduling techniques like **time-sharing and priority-based execution.**
 
 
 
• **Security:**
 
 
• Operating systems implement security measures like **user authentication, access control, and firewalls** to protect data and resources.
 
• Regular updates are provided to address vulnerabilities and enhance security.
 
 
 
• **Virtualization:**
 
 
• Operating systems can support **virtualization**, allowing multiple virtual environments to run on a single physical machine.
 
• It is widely used in cloud computing and server management for resource optimization.

questions.question: Which of the following farming practices is mostly practised in Northeast India and causes soil erosion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shifting agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shifting agriculture**, also known as **Jhum cultivation**, is a traditional farming method practiced in Northeast India, particularly in states like **Assam, Nagaland, and Mizoram**.
 
• Farmers clear forested land by cutting and burning vegetation (**slash-and-burn method**) and use the ash as fertilizer for crops.
 
• This practice leads to severe **soil erosion** due to the removal of vegetation cover, exposing the soil to heavy rainfall and wind.
 
• Shifting agriculture results in the loss of soil nutrients over time, leading to the degradation of land and reduced agricultural productivity.
 
• After a few years, the land is abandoned, and farmers move to another area, repeating the cycle, which further contributes to deforestation and environmental concerns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil Erosion:**

 
 
• It refers to the removal of the topsoil layer due to natural forces like wind and water or human activities such as deforestation and farming.
 
• Soil erosion reduces fertility, destroys agricultural land, and affects water quality in nearby rivers and streams.
 
 
 
• **Terrace Farming:**
 
 
• This is a sustainable agricultural practice where crops are grown on stepped terraces built into hillsides to prevent soil erosion and water runoff.
 
• It is widely practiced in hilly regions, such as in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, but is not the main method used in Northeast India.
 
 
 
• **Mixed Farming:**
 
 
• Involves growing crops and raising livestock simultaneously on the same farm.
 
• It does not involve practices that lead to significant soil erosion.
 
 
 
• **Deforestation:**
 
 
• Shifting agriculture contributes to deforestation as large areas of forests are cleared for farming.
 
• Deforestation leads to loss of biodiversity, disruption of ecosystems, and increased carbon emissions.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major river of the Indus basin system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ravi** is one of the major rivers of the Indus basin system, flowing through India and Pakistan.
 
• The river originates in the **Kullu hills of Himachal Pradesh, India**, and flows westward before entering Pakistan.
 
• It is an important tributary of the Indus River and plays a significant role in the irrigation systems in both countries.
 
• The Ravi River is historically significant, being mentioned in ancient texts like the Rigveda and associated with the region of Punjab.
 
• Under the **Indus Waters Treaty (1960)**, the Ravi is allocated to India for utilization of its waters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus River System**

 
 
• The Indus River System consists of six main rivers: Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej.
 
• These rivers originate in the Himalayas and serve as lifelines for agriculture in northern India and Pakistan.
 
• The system is governed by the **Indus Waters Treaty (1960)**, signed between India and Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Indus Waters Treaty (1960)**
 
 
• The treaty was brokered by the World Bank to resolve water-sharing disputes between India and Pakistan.
 
• Under the treaty, India has control over the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej), while Pakistan controls the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab).
 
 
 
• **Punjab Region**
 
 
• The name "Punjab" translates to "Land of Five Rivers," referring to Ravi, Beas, Sutlej, Chenab, and Jhelum.
 
• The region is agriculturally rich, largely due to the extensive irrigation supported by the Indus River System.
 
 
 
• **Ravi River's Historical Significance**
 
 
• The Ravi River was central to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• It flows near the historic city of Lahore, Pakistan, and has cultural importance in the region.

questions.question: What is the ratio of the angles subtended by a chord at the centre of a circle to the angle subtended at any point on the circumference of the circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the standard **degree measure theorem** of circles, the angle subtended by an arc or chord at the **centre** is always twice the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the **circumference**.

Let the angle subtended at the circumference be θ.

Then, the angle subtended at the centre is 2θ.

Required Ratio = Angle at Centre : Angle at Circumference = 2θ : θ = 2 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ A circle with **centre O**.

⇒ A **chord AB** subtending an angle ∠AOB at the centre **O**.

⇒ The same chord subtends an angle ∠ACB at point **C** on the circumference.

**Theorem Used:**

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre of a circle is twice the angle subtended by it at any point on the circumference.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/065a2d93c669ae2b48f6c0f63f2e98335f0c24d6f81008d7abc12f7638591eca.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the angle subtended at the circumference be ∠ACB = θ

⇒ According to the theorem, the angle subtended at the centre is ∠AOB = 2 × ∠ACB

⇒ ∠AOB = 2θ

⇒ Required Ratio = ∠AOB : ∠ACB

⇒ Ratio = 2θ : θ

⇒ Ratio = 2 : 1

**Explanation of Incorrect Options:**

⇒ **Option (1) 3 : 1** is incorrect because the central angle is exactly double, not triple, the inscribed angle.

⇒ **Option (2) 1 : 3** is incorrect because the central angle must be larger than the inscribed angle, making a ratio less than 1 impossible.

⇒ **Option (3) 1 : 2** is incorrect because this represents the ratio of the angle at the circumference to the angle at the centre, which is the reverse of the requested order.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle in a Semicircle

An angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is always a right angle (90°), which is half of the 180° straight angle at the centre.

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same chord or arc at different points on the same segment of the circumference are always equal.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral always sum up to 180° (they are supplementary).</p

questions.question: What happens if an Indian citizen voluntarily becomes a citizen of another country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Their Indian citizenship ends automatically**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the **Indian Citizenship Act, 1955**, Indian citizenship is automatically terminated when an Indian citizen voluntarily acquires the citizenship of another country.
 
• India follows the principle of **single citizenship**, meaning that dual citizenship is not allowed under Indian law.
 
• An individual acquiring foreign citizenship must **surrender their Indian passport** as it becomes invalid after acquiring foreign nationality.
 
• The government of India issues an **Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card** to eligible individuals of Indian origin, which provides certain privileges but is not equivalent to dual citizenship.
 
• Section 9(1) of the Indian Citizenship Act explicitly states that **Indian citizenship ceases automatically** upon acquiring foreign citizenship voluntarily.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Citizenship Act, 1955**

 
 
• This act governs the acquisition, termination, and supplementary provisions of Indian citizenship.
 
• It provides five modes of acquiring citizenship: by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
 
• It also lays down the grounds for the termination and deprivation of citizenship under specific conditions.
 
 
 
• **Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Card**
 
 
• The OCI card is issued to foreign nationals of Indian origin, allowing them to visit, live, or work in India indefinitely.
 
• It is not equivalent to Indian citizenship, and OCI cardholders cannot vote, hold government office, or purchase agricultural land in India.
 
• The scheme was introduced in 2005 to strengthen the bond between India and its diaspora.
 
 
 
• **Dual Citizenship**
 
 
• Dual citizenship refers to a situation where an individual is a legal citizen of two countries simultaneously.
 
• India does not allow dual citizenship; instead, it provides the OCI card as an alternative for individuals of Indian origin.
 
 
 
• **Surrender Certificate**
 
 
• Indian citizens who acquire foreign nationality must obtain a surrender certificate for their Indian passport.
 
• This certificate is required for availing of consular services and applying for an OCI card.

questions.question: In which order did Mendeleev arrange the elements in his periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increasing atomic mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dmitri Mendeleev arranged the elements in his periodic table based on their **increasing atomic mass**.
 
• He grouped elements with similar chemical properties into vertical columns called **groups**.
 
• Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table to **predict the existence of undiscovered elements** and their properties.
 
• The periodic table was published in **1869**, marking a significant advancement in the study of chemistry.
 
• Although atomic mass was the primary criterion, Mendeleev occasionally altered the arrangement to ensure elements with similar properties were aligned correctly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table:**

 
 
• A tabular arrangement of chemical elements organized by their **atomic number, electron configuration, and recurring chemical properties**.
 
• The modern periodic table is based on the **Moseley’s concept of increasing atomic number**, rather than atomic mass.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• The total mass of protons and neutrons in an atom's nucleus.
 
• Mendeleev used atomic mass as a criterion because atomic numbers were unknown at the time.
 
 
 
• **Predictions Made by Mendeleev:**
 
 
• Mendeleev successfully predicted the properties of elements like **gallium (eka-aluminum)** and **germanium (eka-silicon)**.
 
• These predictions were later confirmed with the discovery of these elements.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Mendeleev’s Table:**
 
 
• Some elements were placed out of order based on atomic mass to align with chemical properties.
 
• The periodic table did not account for the existence of **isotopes**, which have the same atomic number but different atomic masses.

In each of the words, each vowel is changed to the letter immediately following it in the English alphabetical order and each consonant is changed to the letter immediately preceding in the English alphabetical order.

Thus, the new clusters formed are:

DIE → CJF

CUP → BVO

BOX → APW

ASK → BRJ

In these clusters, the ones without any vowel (A, E, I, O, U) are:

CJF, BVO, APW, BRJ

Thus, 2 cluster of letter without any vowel CJF, BRJ

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: When x is added to each of 26, 40, 22 and 34, then the numbers so obtained, in this order, are in proportion. Then, if 4x : y :: y : (7x-6), and y > 0, what is the value of y?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For numbers **a, b, c, d** to be in proportion after adding **x**: **x = (ad − bc) ÷ ((a + d) − (b + c))**.

Here a = 26, b = 40, c = 22, d = 34.

x = (26 × 34 − 40 × 22) ÷ ((26 + 34) − (40 + 22)) = (884 − 880) ÷ (60 − 62) = 4 ÷ (−2) = −2.

Mean proportional **y² = 4x × (7x − 6)** ⇒ y² = 4(−2) × (7(−2) − 6) = −8 × (−20) = 160. (Check values: 26−2=24, 40−2=38, 22−2=20, 34−2=32. 24/38 ≠ 20/32).

Correcting calculation: x = (bc − ad) ÷ ((a+d) − (b+c)) = (880 − 884) ÷ (60 − 62) = −4 ÷ −2 = 2. **x = 2**. Then y² = 4(2) × (7(2) − 6) = 8 × 8 = 64 ⇒ **y = 8**.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

⇒ 884 + 26x + 34x + x² = 880 + 22x + 40x + x²

⇒ 884 + 60x = 880 + 62x

⇒ 62x − 60x = 884 − 880

⇒ 2x = 4 ⇒ **x = 2**

⇒ Given 4x : y :: y : (7x − 6)

⇒ y² = 4x × (7x − 6)

⇒ y² = 4(2) × (7 × 2 − 6)

⇒ y² = 8 × (14 − 6)

⇒ y² = 8 × 8 = 64

⇒ y = √64 = 8 (as y > 0)

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is √(ab). It is also written as a : b :: b : c where b² = ac.

For four numbers a, b, c, d to be in proportion, the product of extremes must equal the product of means (ad = bc).

questions.question: The marked price of a desk is ₹7,725, which is 25% above the cost price. It is sold at a discount of 4% on the marked price. Find the profit percentage.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net profit percentage = **a − b − (a × b) ÷ 100**, where a is the markup percentage and b is the discount percentage.

Here, markup percentage (a) = **25%** and discount percentage (b) = **4%**.

Net Profit% = 25 − 4 − (25 × 4) ÷ 100

Net Profit% = 21 − 100 ÷ 100 = 21 − 1 = **20%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Marked Price (MP) = **₹7,725**, Markup = **25%**, Discount = **4%**.
**Formulas:** Profit% = ((SP − CP) ÷ CP) × 100 | SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100 | CP = MP × 100 ÷ (100 + Markup%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a95ba29f91d38dfc7b327c53ea341e10ffb08554304c93a4494a3bfe093f2e34.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100 units.
⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 25% of 100 = 125 units.
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = MP − 4% of MP = 125 − (4 ÷ 100 × 125) = 125 − 5 = 120 units.
⇒ **Profit** = SP − CP = 120 − 100 = 20 units.
⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (20 ÷ 100) × 100 = **20%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP and MP

The ratio of CP to MP can be calculated as CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

Successive Percentage Change

Profit% is the resultant of markup (increase) and discount (decrease) applied successively on the Cost Price.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of cache memory in a computer?

options.text: To store frequently accessed data for quick retrieval

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To store frequently accessed data for quick retrieval**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cache memory** is a small-sized, high-speed memory located close to the CPU, designed to store **frequently accessed data and instructions**.
 
• It reduces the time required to access data from the main memory (RAM), thereby **improving system performance**.
 
• Cache operates at a much faster speed compared to RAM, enabling the **CPU to retrieve essential data quickly** without delays.
 
• Modern processors often include multiple levels of cache, such as **L1, L2, and L3 cache**, each with varying speeds and sizes for optimized performance.
 
• By minimizing the need for frequent access to slower main memory, cache memory plays a crucial role in **enhancing processing efficiency**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Levels of Cache Memory:**

 
 
• **L1 Cache:** Closest to the CPU, the smallest and fastest type of cache.
 
• **L2 Cache:** Larger and slightly slower than L1, typically located on the CPU chip.
 
• **L3 Cache:** Shared among CPU cores, larger but slower than L1 and L2.
 
 
 
• **Cache Hit and Miss:**
 
 
• A **cache hit** occurs when the CPU finds the required data in the cache, resulting in faster access.
 
• A **cache miss** happens when the data is not in the cache, forcing the CPU to retrieve it from main memory.
 
 
 
• **Cache Replacement Policies:**
 
 
• Techniques like **Least Recently Used (LRU)**, **First In First Out (FIFO)**, and **Random Replacement** determine which data to replace in cache when it's full.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Cache and RAM:**
 
 
• Cache memory is faster but smaller in size compared to RAM.
 
• RAM stores larger data temporarily, while cache focuses on frequently accessed data for rapid retrieval.
 
 
 
• **Modern Applications:**
 
 
• Cache memory is crucial in applications like gaming, video editing, and database management systems for **enhancing processing speeds**.

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of 25 real numbers is 110. If 10 numbers are increased by 12(1)/(2) each, another 10 numbers are increased by 15 each and the remaining 5 numbers are unaltered, then the new value of the arithmetic mean is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Net increase** in the sum = (10 × 12.5) + (10 × 15) + (5 × 0)

**Net increase** = 125 + 150 + 0 = 275

**Increase in mean** = Total Increase ÷ Total Numbers = 275 ÷ 25 = 11

**New arithmetic mean** = Old Mean + Increase = 110 + 11 = 121

**∴ The correct answer is 121.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers (n) = 25

Initial **Arithmetic Mean** = 110

**Formula Used:**

New Mean = (Original Sum + Total Change) ÷ Total Numbers

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9c7dee6c089f3ef13acc78f9a1c45fe5a131678971df8ef89f410b1d9a29d661.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Original Sum** of 25 numbers = 25 × 110 = 2750

⇒ **Increase** from first 10 numbers = 10 × 12.5 = 125

⇒ **Increase** from next 10 numbers = 10 × 15 = 150

⇒ **Total Increase** = 125 + 150 + (5 × 0) = 275

⇒ **New Total Sum** = 2750 + 275 = 3025

⇒ **New Arithmetic Mean** = 3025 ÷ 25

⇒ **New Arithmetic Mean** = 121

**∴ The correct answer is 121.**

**__Additional Information__**

Linear Property of Mean

If a constant **k** is added to every observation in a data set, the **new mean** is the **original mean + k**.

Total Sum Formula

The sum of all observations is always equal to **Mean × Number of observations** (Sum = x¯ × n).

Weighted Average

When groups are changed differently, the **net change in mean** is (Σ nᵢ × cᵢ) ÷ N, where cᵢ is the change in each group.</p

questions.question: AB is parallel to CD. A transversal PQ intersects AB and CD at E and F, respectively, and ∠PEB = 56°. G is a point between AB and CD such that ∠BEG = 32° and ∠GFE = 47°. What is the measure of ∠EGF?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

∠BEF = 180° − ∠PEB = 180° − 56° = 124° (Linear pair)

∠GEF = ∠BEF − ∠BEG = 124° − 32° = 92°

In ▵EGF, sum of angles = 180°

∠EGF = 180° − (∠GEF + ∠GFE) = 180° − (92° + 47°) = 41°

**∴ The correct answer is 41°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **AB || CD**, **transversal PQ** intersects them at **E** and **F**. **∠PEB = 56°**, **∠BEG = 32°**, and **∠GFE = 47°**.

**Formula Used:** Linear pair property (sum = 180°) and Angle Sum Property of a triangle (sum = 180°).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/21336634dfba58e0dee75adbbf3b46c458b1026b3ada460dbda6252dfd3093f1.png] 

⇒ Since **PQ** is a straight line, **∠PEB + ∠BEF = 180°** (Linear pair)

⇒ 56° + ∠BEF = 180°

⇒ ∠BEF = 180° − 56° = 124°

⇒ From the figure, **∠BEF = ∠BEG + ∠GEF**

⇒ 124° = 32° + ∠GEF

⇒ ∠GEF = 124° − 32° = 92°

⇒ In **▵EGF**, **∠GEF + ∠GFE + ∠EGF = 180°**

⇒ 92° + 47° + ∠EGF = 180°

⇒ 139° + ∠EGF = 180°

⇒ ∠EGF = 180° − 139° = 41°

**∴ The correct answer is 41°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Parallel Lines and Transversals

When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, corresponding angles are equal, and alternate interior angles are equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.

Linear Pair Axiom

If a ray stands on a line, then the sum of two adjacent angles so formed is 180°.</p

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cone is 5400π cm², and the diameter of its base is 144 cm. Find the height (in cm) of the cone.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Radius (r) = 144 ÷ 2 = 72 cm

CSA = πrl ⇒ 5400π = π × 72 × l

l = 5400 ÷ 72 = 75 cm

Using Pythagorean triplet (7, 24, 25) × 3 → (21, 72, 75)

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 5400π cm²

**Diameter** = 144 cm ⇒ **Radius (r)** = 72 cm

**Formula Used:**

CSA of Cone = πrl

Slant height (l) = √(h² + r²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3cf7e7f1262c085f0ba9083b80c202e580ba35a8e08b797a76a0c5a986e52c3b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ π × 72 × l = 5400π

⇒ l = 5400 ÷ 72

⇒ l = 75 cm

⇒ h² = l² − r²

⇒ h² = 75² − 72²

⇒ h² = (75 − 72)(75 + 72)

⇒ h² = 3 × 147

⇒ h² = 441

⇒ h = √441 = 21 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cone

TSA = πr(l + r), which includes the curved area and the circular base area.

Volume of Cone

Volume = (1/3)πr²h, which is exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height.

Slant Height Relation

In a right circular cone, l² = h² + r² based on the **Pythagoras Theorem**.</p

questions.question: What was the Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) in India according to the Sample Registration System (SRS), 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30 per 1000 live births**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the **Sample Registration System (SRS) 2019**, the **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)** in India was **30 per 1000 live births**.
 
• IMR represents the number of deaths of infants under one year of age per 1000 live births in a given year.
 
• India has witnessed a consistent decline in IMR over the years due to improvements in healthcare, sanitation, and immunization coverage.
 
• The IMR in rural areas was higher at **34 per 1000 live births** compared to urban areas, which recorded **20 per 1000 live births**.
 
• This decline in IMR aligns with the government’s efforts under programs like **National Health Mission (NHM)** and **Intensified Mission Indradhanush**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sample Registration System (SRS):**

 
 
• SRS is a demographic survey conducted in India by the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner**.
 
• It provides reliable annual estimates of birth rates, death rates, and other fertility and mortality indicators.
 
 
 
• **Neonatal Mortality Rate (NMR):**
 
 
• NMR refers to the number of deaths of newborns within the first 28 days of life per 1000 live births.
 
• India’s NMR in 2019 stood at **22 per 1000 live births**, as per SRS data.
 
 
 
• **National Health Mission (NHM):**
 
 
• The NHM aims to improve healthcare access and outcomes, particularly for women and children.
 
• It includes initiatives like Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) and Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakaram (JSSK).
 
 
 
• **Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI):**
 
 
• IMI aims to achieve full immunization coverage for children under two years and pregnant women.
 
• It targets unvaccinated and partially vaccinated children in underserved areas.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG):**
 
 
• India is committed to reducing IMR and NMR in alignment with SDG 3, which focuses on ensuring healthy lives and promoting well-being for all at all ages.

questions.question: What was the major impact of penicillin's discovery?

options.text: First antiviral drug for Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)
First vaccine for prevention of smallpox
First effective antibiotic against bacterial infections
First drug for Rabies prevention and cure

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First effective antibiotic against bacterial infections**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Penicillin**, discovered by **Alexander Fleming in 1928**, was the first antibiotic that proved to be highly effective against bacterial infections.
 
• The discovery marked the beginning of the modern era of antibiotics, revolutionizing the treatment of bacterial diseases such as pneumonia, syphilis, and strep throat.
 
• During World War II, penicillin was mass-produced and saved countless lives by treating infections in wounded soldiers.
 
• Penicillin works by inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis, making it effective against a wide range of Gram-positive bacteria.
 
• Its discovery earned Alexander Fleming, Howard Florey, and Ernst Boris Chain the **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1945**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Antibiotics:**

 
 
• Substances that kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria without harming the host organism.
 
• Penicillin was the first antibiotic discovered, followed by others like streptomycin, tetracycline, and erythromycin.
 
• Overuse or misuse of antibiotics can lead to antibiotic resistance, a significant global health concern.
 
 
 
• **Alexander Fleming's Discovery:**
 
 
• Fleming observed that a mold, later identified as *Penicillium notatum*, inhibited bacterial growth on a petri dish.
 
• This serendipitous discovery laid the foundation for the development of antibiotics.
 
 
 
• **Mass Production of Penicillin:**
 
 
• During World War II, efforts led by Howard Florey and Ernst Chain enabled large-scale production of penicillin.
 
• This breakthrough ensured the availability of the drug for treating battlefield infections and saving civilian lives.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Medicine:**
 
 
• Penicillin reduced mortality rates from bacterial infections and transformed medical practices worldwide.
 
• It is considered one of the most significant discoveries in medical history.

questions.question: Suppose x : y = 2 : 5; y : z = 4 : 7. If ₹15,120 is distributed among x, y and z, then the amounts received by x, y and z, respectively, are (in ₹):
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combine ratios: **x : y : z** = (2 × 4) : (5 × 4) : (5 × 7) = **8 : 20 : 35**.

Total units = 8 + 20 + 35 = **63 units**.

Value of 1 unit = 15,120 ÷ 63 = **₹240**.

Amounts: x = 8 × 240 = **₹1,920**; y = 20 × 240 = **₹4,800**; z = 35 × 240 = **₹8,400**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1,920, 4,800 and 8,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x : y = 2 : 5 and y : z = 4 : 7. Total Amount = **₹15,120**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6f556313b52b902dde2febb8296ab67272ceca75264faa86a07d5df5c487d425.png] 

⇒ To equalize y: x : y = (2×4) : (5×4) = 8 : 20

⇒ y : z = (4×5) : (7×5) = 20 : 35

⇒ Combined Ratio **x : y : z** = 8 : 20 : 35

⇒ Total Share = 8k + 20k + 35k = 63k

⇒ 63k = 15,120 ⇒ k = 15,120 ÷ 63 = 240

⇒ **x** = 8 × 240 = ₹1,920

⇒ **y** = 20 × 240 = ₹4,800

⇒ **z** = 35 × 240 = ₹8,400

**∴ The correct answer is 1,920, 4,800 and 8,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Combination Rule

To combine a:b and b:c, multiply the terms so that the common variable 'b' has the same numerical value in both ratios.

Proportional Division

If a total amount T is divided in ratio a:b:c, the share of the first part is [a / (a+b+c)] × T.

Verification Tip

Always ensure that the sum of calculated individual shares equals the total given amount (1,920 + 4,800 + 8,400 = 15,120).

questions.question: What is the primary function of the CPU in a computer system ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Execute instructions and process data**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the **primary component of a computer system responsible for executing instructions** provided by software programs.
 
• It performs the essential task of **processing data**, which includes arithmetic operations, logic operations, control functions, and input/output operations.
 
• The CPU consists of three key components: the **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)**, **Control Unit (CU)**, and registers, which help in executing instructions efficiently.
 
• The CPU operates based on the **fetch-decode-execute cycle**, where it retrieves instructions from memory, decodes them, and performs the required operations.
 
• Modern CPUs are equipped with **multiple cores**, enabling parallel processing and significantly improving performance for multitasking and complex computations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU):**

 
 
• The ALU is a fundamental part of the CPU responsible for performing arithmetic operations (e.g., addition, subtraction) and logical operations (e.g., comparisons).
 
• It acts as the computational powerhouse of the CPU.
 
 
 
• **Control Unit (CU):**
 
 
• The CU directs the operation of the processor by interpreting instructions and ensuring that data flows correctly between the CPU and other components.
 
• It coordinates the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
 
 
 
• **Registers:**
 
 
• Registers are small, high-speed storage areas within the CPU that temporarily store data and instructions during processing.
 
• They facilitate quick access to frequently used data.
 
 
 
• **Clock Speed:**
 
 
• Clock speed, measured in GHz (gigahertz), represents the number of cycles a CPU can perform per second.
 
• Higher clock speeds generally result in faster processing but are also influenced by the CPU architecture and core count.
 
 
 
• **Multi-Core Processors:**
 
 
• Modern CPUs often include multiple cores, enabling them to perform multiple tasks simultaneously.
 
• Multi-core processors enhance performance in applications that support parallel computing, such as video editing and gaming.

At constant expenditure, the **Quantity** is inversely proportional to the **Price** per unit.

**Profit** = 40% ⇒ Ratio of **CP : SP** = 100 : 140 = 5 : 7.

Therefore, the ratio of **Quantity (CP) : Quantity (SP)** = 7 : 5.

Given: Selling quantity = 5 chocolates for &8377;1.

Since 5 units = 5 chocolates, then 7 units = **7 chocolates**.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

⇒ Number of chocolates bought for &8377;1 = 1 ÷ (1/7) = **7**.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

questions.question: Rajesh has 156 litres of Oil A and 256 litres of Oil B. He fills a number of identical containers with the two types of oil in a manner that each container has only one type of oil, and all containers are completely filled. What can be the maximum volume (in litres) of each container that Rajesh uses, so that all the oil that Rajesh has, of both the types, can be poured into these containers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **maximum volume** of identical containers, we must find the **HCF (Highest Common Factor)** of the given quantities.

Quantities: 156 and 256.

HCF(156, 256) ⇒ Difference = 256 − 156 = 100.

Factors of 100 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, 100. Checking the largest factor that divides both 156 and 256.

156 is divisible by 4, and 256 is divisible by 4. Larger factors of 100 do not divide 156.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume of **Oil A** = 156 litres

Volume of **Oil B** = 256 litres

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/420350598e7d52d08772551e5d9b85cb2e3fa5351d7d47fa61d2307c8bb51015.png] 

**Calculation:**

To find the **maximum capacity** of each container, calculate the **HCF** of 156 and 256.

Prime factorization of 156:

⇒ 156 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 13 = 2² × 3 × 13

Prime factorization of 256:

⇒ 256 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2⁸

HCF is the product of the lowest powers of common prime factors:

⇒ HCF = 2²

⇒ HCF = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

HCF is the greatest number that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder. It is also known as GCF or GCD.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

LCM is the smallest non-zero common multiple of two or more numbers. Relationship: Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM.

Application in Partitioning

When items need to be divided into the largest possible equal groups or containers without mixing, HCF is always the required value.</p

questions.question: Which of the following best encapsulates the role of an operating system's kernel?

options.text: Managing user accounts and access permissions
Providing the graphical user interface for user interaction

Acting as the core interface between applications and the system hardware

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acting as the core interface between applications and the system hardware**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The kernel is the **central component of an operating system** and serves as the core interface between the system's hardware and its applications.
 
• It manages critical tasks such as **CPU scheduling, memory management, and device control**.
 
• The kernel ensures that multiple programs and processes can run simultaneously by **handling resource allocation and process isolation**.
 
• It provides low-level system services such as **hardware abstraction** and ensures secure and efficient communication between the hardware and software.
 
• Popular kernel types include **monolithic kernels** (e.g., Linux) and **microkernels** (e.g., MINIX), each with distinct advantages in terms of performance and modularity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kernel Modes:**

 
 
• Modern operating systems use two modes: **User Mode** (for running applications) and **Kernel Mode** (for executing system-level tasks).
 
• The kernel operates in Kernel Mode, with unrestricted access to hardware resources and memory.
 
 
 
• **Types of Kernels:**
 
 
• **Monolithic Kernel:** All OS services run in a single large process, providing better performance but less modularity.
 
• **Microkernel:** Only essential services run in the kernel, while others run in user space, enhancing modularity and fault isolation.
 
 
 
• **Memory Management:**
 
 
• The kernel handles memory allocation and ensures that processes do not interfere with each other.
 
• Techniques such as **virtual memory** allow efficient memory utilization.
 
 
 
• **Hardware Abstraction:**
 
 
• The kernel provides a hardware abstraction layer (HAL) to shield applications from hardware-specific details.
 
• This abstraction makes the OS adaptable to different hardware platforms.
 
 
 
• **Process Management:**
 
 
• The kernel creates, schedules, and terminates processes.
 
• It ensures fairness in CPU time distribution and prevents deadlocks through mechanisms like **semaphores** and **mutexes**.

questions.question:
Simplify the following.

(2x +3)² − (x + 1)².
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Difference of Squares** identity: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

Let a = 2x + 3 and b = x + 1.

Sum (a + b) = 2x + 3 + x + 1 = 3x + 4.

Difference (a − b) = 2x + 3 − (x + 1) = x + 2.

Multiply factors: (3x + 4)(x + 2) = 3x² + 6x + 4x + 8 = 3x² + 10x + 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 3x² + 10x + 8.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The expression to **simplify** is (2x + 3)² − (x + 1)².

**Formula Used:** (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

⇒ Expand the first term: (2x + 3)² = (2x)² + 2(2x)(3) + 3² = 4x² + 12x + 9

⇒ Expand the second term: (x + 1)² = x² + 2(x)(1) + 1² = x² + 2x + 1

⇒ Substitute back: (4x² + 12x + 9) − (x² + 2x + 1)

⇒ Distribute the negative sign: 4x² + 12x + 9 − x² − 2x − 1

⇒ Combine **like terms**: (4x² − x²) + (12x − 2x) + (9 − 1)

⇒ Result: 3x² + 10x + 8

**∴ The correct answer is 3x² + 10x + 8.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

Standard identities like (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b² are essential for polynomial expansion.

Difference of Squares

The formula a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) is often faster for simplifying subtractions of two squared terms.

Like Terms

Polynomial simplification requires grouping terms with the same **exponent** and variable (e.g., all x² terms together).</p

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest, compounded annually and the simple interest if ₹47,100 is deposited at 9% rate of interest per annum for 2 years is:

For a period of **2 years**, the difference between **Compound Interest (CI)** and **Simple Interest (SI)** is given by the formula:

**Difference (D) = P × (R/100)²**

**Step 3: Calculate the Difference**

questions.question: At what rate of interest (rounded off to two decimal places) per year will a sum of money double itself in 12 years on simple interest?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a sum to become **n times** itself at **Simple Interest**, use the shortcut: **Rate (R) = (n − 1) ÷ T × 100**.

Here, the sum **doubles**, so **n = 2**, and time **T = 12 years**.

R = (2 − 1) ÷ 12 × 100

R = 100 ÷ 12 = 8.333...

**∴ The correct answer is 8.33%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (T) = **12 years**

Final Amount (A) = **2 × Principal (P)**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b100a3effb31f726626d88e2ff34d32487ceb81bea273cc99252cc2986285709.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Principal (P)** = ₹100

⇒ Since the sum doubles, **Amount (A)** = 2 × 100 = **₹200**

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** = Amount − Principal = 200 − 100 = **₹100**

⇒ Substitute in the formula: 100 = (100 × R × 12) ÷ 100

⇒ 100 = 12 × R

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 12

⇒ R = 8.333... ≈ **8.33%**

**∴ The correct answer is 8.33%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Definition

Simple interest is calculated only on the **original principal** amount for every time period.

Sum tripling rule

If a sum triples (n=3), the interest gained is 2P, so **R × T = 200**.

Amount calculation

Final Amount (A) = Principal (P) + SI = **P[1 + (R × T) ÷ 100]**.

questions.question: From a taxi stand, two cabs start at a speed of 74 km/hr at an interval of 28 minutes, both cabs travelling in the same direction. A man coming in the opposite direction towards the taxi stand meets the cabs at an interval of 10 minutes. Find the speed (in km/hr) of the man.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
The **distance** covered by the **cab** in the **remaining time** (28 − 10 = 18 min) is equal to the distance covered by the **man** in 10 minutes.

Ratio of **Time** (Cab : Man) = 18 : 10 = 9 : 5

Ratio of **Speed** (Cab : Man) = 5 : 9

Speed of **Man** = (74 ÷ 5) × 9 = 14.8 × 9 = 133.2 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 133.2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9123432ef54cbdb43ca6ed0858e5a0458aa254360fcc6be57f5feac018af5f16.png] 
**Given:** Speed of **Cab** (S꜀) = 74 km/hr, Time Interval of Cabs (Tᵢ) = 28 min, Meeting Interval (Tₘ) = 10 min.

**Formula:** S꜀ × (Tᵢ − Tₘ) = Sₘ × Tₘ

⇒ Distance between two cabs = 74 × (28/60) km

⇒ In 10 minutes, the **Man** and the **Cab** cover this distance together (Relative Speed).

⇒ (74 + Sₘ) × (10/60) = 74 × (28/60)

⇒ (74 + Sₘ) × 10 = 74 × 28

⇒ 74 + Sₘ = (74 × 28) ÷ 10

⇒ 74 + Sₘ = 2072 ÷ 10 = 207.2

⇒ Sₘ = 207.2 − 74 = 133.2 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 133.2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move towards each other, their **relative speed** is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Sound and Echo Logic

This problem follows the same logic as **bullets fired** at intervals where a person hears the sounds at different intervals due to motion.

Time-Speed Inverseness

For a constant distance, speed is **inversely proportional** to time (S ∝ 1/T).</p

__
 
• **Ingestion** is the first step in holozoic nutrition, **where food is taken into the body for further processing**.
 
• It involves the intake of solid or liquid food through specialized structures such as the mouth or oral cavity in complex organisms.
 
• Ingestion enables organisms to acquire nutrients essential for their survival and growth.
 
• Holozoic nutrition is characteristic of most animals, including humans, and consists of multiple stages such as ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation, and egestion.
 
• This step is critical for initiating the process of converting complex organic substances into simpler, absorbable forms for energy and cellular function.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Digestion:** The biochemical process that breaks down complex food molecules into simpler substances using enzymes.
 
• **Absorption:** The process where digested nutrients are absorbed into the bloodstream or cells for distribution throughout the body.
 
• **Assimilation:** The utilization of absorbed nutrients by cells to produce energy and build cellular structures.
 
• **Egestion:** The expulsion of undigested food and waste materials from the body after the completion of digestion.

questions.question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank of 3700 litres in 9 hours and 6 hours, respectively. If they are opened together, how many hours will they take to fill an empty tank of 6400 litres?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 3700 ÷ 9 litres/hr.

Efficiency of **Pipe B** = 3700 ÷ 6 litres/hr.

Combined efficiency = (3700 × (2 + 3)) ÷ 18 = (3700 × 5) ÷ 18 = 18500 ÷ 18 = 9250 ÷ 9 litres/hr.

Time to fill 6400 litres = 6400 ÷ (9250 ÷ 9) = (6400 × 9) ÷ 9250 = (640 × 9) ÷ 925 = 1152 ÷ 185 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1152/185 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 **B**

**Total Capacity** of target tank = 6400 litres.

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe A** (EA) = 3700/9 litres/hr.

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe B** (EB) = 3700/6 = 1850/3 litres/hr.

⇒ Combined Efficiency (EA₊B) = (3700/9) + (1850/3) = (3700 + 5550)/9 = 9250/9 litres/hr.

⇒ Time taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 6400 ÷ (9250/9) = (6400 × 9) ÷ 9250

⇒ Time = (640 × 9) ÷ 925 = 5760 ÷ 925

⇒ Time = 1152/185 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1152/185 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Efficiency Formula

When two pipes work together, their **total efficiency** is the sum of their individual efficiencies: Eₜₒₜₐₗ = E₁ + E₂.

Time and Work Relationship

The **time** taken to complete a task is inversely proportional to the **efficiency**: Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency.

Inlet vs Outlet Pipes

**Inlet pipes** have positive efficiency (add water), while **outlet pipes** (leaks) have negative efficiency (remove water).</p

questions.question: In 2025, which state launched a groundbreaking initiative aimed at eradicating mother to-child transmission of HIV, syphilis, and Hepatitis B by 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2025, the state of **West Bengal** launched an innovative program aimed at eradicating mother-to-child transmission of HIV, syphilis, and Hepatitis B by the year 2026.
 
• This initiative aligns with global efforts under the **World Health Organization’s (WHO) elimination strategy** for these diseases.
 
• West Bengal became the **first state in India** to implement such a comprehensive program focusing on maternal and child health.
 
• The program includes widespread testing, awareness campaigns, and free treatment for affected mothers to ensure the health of newborns.
 
• Specialized healthcare facilities were set up in collaboration with national and international health organizations to support this initiative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mother-to-Child Transmission (MTCT):**

 
 
• MTCT refers to the transmission of diseases such as HIV, syphilis, or Hepatitis B from an infected mother to her child during pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding.
 
• It is a major public health issue, especially in low- and middle-income countries.
 
 
 
• **HIV Elimination Efforts:**
 
 
• The **UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets** aim to ensure that 95% of people with HIV know their status, 95% are on treatment, and 95% achieve viral suppression by 2030.
 
• India has been actively working to reduce HIV prevalence through initiatives like the National AIDS Control Program.
 
 
 
• **Syphilis Testing and Treatment:**
 
 
• Early detection and treatment of syphilis during pregnancy can prevent congenital syphilis, which can lead to severe complications in newborns.
 
• Penicillin remains the most effective treatment for syphilis.
 
 
 
• **Hepatitis B Prevention:**
 
 
• Hepatitis B vaccines are highly effective in preventing transmission and are recommended for all newborns within 24 hours of birth.
 
• India’s Universal Immunization Program includes free Hepatitis B vaccination for children.
